go_file: # Go test functions from tests/fixtures/go/test-inventory.tsv that match
# no Rust #[test] by name (Q-INVENTORY-GUARD). Each was read against
# the Go test at the pinned SHA in P9 · S1. `ported` names the Rust tests
# that port it under another name; `excused` has none, and its ref says
# why. Refs are Q- entries or paths under
# TestListsCommandEntryIgnoresProse: Tests a Go test helper that parsed Cobra's help text; the Rust help tests read the registry and clap's tree.
# TestLinkTimeVersionInjection: Ported as `make stamp-check`, a CI step in test.yml (a stamped rebuild inside `make test` costs more than it proves); not a #[test].
# TestMain: Go's TestMain is the fake-editor re-entry, the scrypt hook, and a cleanup of the binary it built. Cargo builds the binary, so the last has nothing to port.
# TestResolveBuildInfoFallsBackToModuleVersion: Go's runtime/debug embedded build info has no Rust equivalent; unset goes straight to dev/unknown (resolve_build_info_without_stamps).
# TestWriteFileReplacesRatherThanTruncatesInPlace: Unix only: Windows refuses to rename over a file with an open handle, so the old-handle probe can't run there.
# TestUnregisteredCodeStringsAsItsNumber: An out-of-range Code can't be built; what carries over is that every code renders as a non-empty name.
# TestWrapNilIsNil: Compile-time: a code is attached only by converting an error value, so there is no nil to wrap.
# TestReleaseOnANilLockIsANoOp: Rust has no nil lock; the analogue is an explicit release followed by the Drop.
# TestUnknownRoleValuePanicsInAllThreeSelectors: Role is a closed enum: an unknown role can't be constructed and the matches are exhaustive.
# TestInsertDuplicateFieldNameIsUsageErrorBeforeUnlock: The five --field refusals are one table test through the CLI, each case asserting Usage, no unlock, and its own reason.
# TestPrompterRefusesAMethodItCannotSatisfy: Kind is #[non_exhaustive] with one variant: the wildcard refusal arm is untestable until a second Kind exists.
# TestDecryptWithAClosedIdentityFails: Compile-time: a compile_fail doctest on crypt::decrypt (a dropped Identity can't be passed), paired with a compiling sibling.
# TestEncryptRefusesAZeroValueRecipient: Recipient has private fields and no Default; compile_fail doctests on Recipient prove it can't be built by hand.
# TestUnknownValueNodeDefaultFallsBackToLibraryEncoding: Rust's unknown values are a closed node type and the match is exhaustive: no exotic type reaches the emitter.
# TestUnlockRejectsAPrompterAnsweringTheWrongKind: UnlockResponse's variants mirror Kind's one to one, so a mismatched answer can't be built until a second Kind exists.
# TestIdentityCopiesShareOneClose: Compile-time: Identity is not Clone (compile_fail doctest in identity.rs).
# TestNilIdentityCloseDoesNotPanic: Rust has no nil Identity.
# TestUsingAnIdentityAfterCloseFails: Compile-time: a dropped Identity can't be used (compile_fail doctest in identity.rs).
# TestZeroIdentityIsSafeToCloseAndUnusable: Identity has no zero value: it can't be constructed outside the library.
# TestGenerateDrawsFromCryptoRandNotMathRand: Go's source scan also checks for rand.Int over a modulo; Rust proves the unbiased draw behaviorally.
# TestSyncReportsAPushEvenWhenNothingWasSent: Go pinned its bug F2; gage-rs fixes it, so the assertion is flipped.
# TestRemoteStateStringCoversAllStatesAndUnknown: Its state(99) half is struck: a Rust enum can't hold an out-of-range value.
# TestClassifyPassesNilThrough: The classifiers take an error, not an Option of one: there is no nil to pass.
# TestRecipientListMatchesConfigExactly: The listing matching the config, then after an add and after a remove.
# TestVerifyReadsNeitherIdentityNorPrompter: The signature takes neither, so the compiler proves half; the no-identity-file case is what's left.
# TestReadRejectsALineLongerThanTheScannerCanBuffer: Decided in M9a: no line cap is invented to match bufio.Scanner's; an overlong line comes back whole, never truncated or dropped.
# TestTerminalPrompterOfWalksDecoratorChains: gage-rs never unwraps a prompter to reach the terminal one; every_wrapper_passes_through_each_method_it_does_not_answer replaces it.
# TestLogAndHeadCommitterTimeOnARepoWithNoCommitsYet: Split: the Log half landed in P6 · M12a, the HeadCommitterTime half in P7 · E3.
# TestRecoverDeviceZeroesTheSecretItWasHanded: Ownership moves in, so the zeroing is the drop's; what's left to prove is the by-value signature and that nothing copies it.
